repos.brief:
**What it does:** A collection of agent skills that teach Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode how to read and write Obsidian-specific formats — Markdown with wikilinks, Bases `.base` files, JSON Canvas, and vault CLI operations.

**Why now:** The repo gained 8,333 stars this week, coinciding with the apparent launch of the Agent Skills specification (`agentskills.io`) as a cross-agent standard, making this an early real-world skill pack for that emerging ecosystem.

**Build with it:** Drop these skills into Claude Code via `npx skills add` and wire an agent to your Obsidian vault to automate note generation from CSV data using the Knap skill, or scrape and clean web content directly into vault markdown via the Defuddle skill.

**What it does:** Ponytail is a JavaScript plugin/skill for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, and ~18 others) that injects YAGNI-style constraints, steering agents toward minimal solutions—replacing a five-file date picker with a single `<input type="date">`.

**Why now:** The repo spiked nearly 7,000 stars this week, coinciding with broader community frustration about Claude Code over-engineering simple tasks and inflating token costs in agentic sessions.

**Build with it:** Drop the npm package (`@dietrichgebert/ponytail`) into your Claude Code or Cursor config as an agent skill, then point it at any feature branch where token spend is high—it targets the over-built tasks first and leaves already-minimal code untouched.

**What it does:** ECC is an agent harness configuration layer that adds persistent skills, memory, instincts, and security guardrails to AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, and Cursor via structured prompt and config files.

**Why now:** Claude Code's rapid adoption as a terminal-native agentic coding tool has triggered a wave of teams needing shared, repeatable agent behavior across codebases — ECC's MCP-compatible harness addresses that gap directly as the ecosystem matures.

**Build with it:** Drop ECC's CLAUDE.md and agent skill configs into a monorepo's root, wire it to your Claude Code or Cursor workspace, and enforce consistent security policies and research-first workflows across all contributors without per-developer setup.

**What it does:** Hermes Agent is a Python-based AI agent framework from Nous Research with a built-in learning loop — it creates and self-improves skills from experience, maintains cross-session memory via FTS5 search and LLM summarization, and runs across seven terminal backends including Modal and Daytona serverless environments.

**Why now:** The repo is spiking at +2,354 stars this week, coinciding with Nous Research's push around their Hermes model lineage and growing community interest in persistent, self-improving agents as alternatives to ephemeral session-based tools like Claude Code and Codex.

**Build with it:** Wire your existing OpenRouter or custom endpoint via `hermes model` (no code changes), then use the RPC-based subagent API to parallelize multi-step pipelines — for example, spawning isolated subagents for concurrent code review, test generation, and deployment checks within a single CI workflow.

**What it does:** Graphify parses any codebase—plus its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs—into a queryable knowledge graph using local deterministic AST parsing via tree-sitter, with every edge explicitly explained and no vector store required.

**Why now:** The repo is trending at nearly 2,000 stars this week, coinciding with the rapid adoption of agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI) that benefit directly from structured codebase context over raw file search.

**Build with it:** Drop in the `/graphify` MCP skill to Claude Code or Cursor, point it at a monorepo, and wire the resulting knowledge graph into a GraphRAG retrieval step so your agent resolves cross-file call chains and schema dependencies before generating diffs.

**What it does:** Taste-Skill is a collection of portable agent skills (prompt/config files) that steer AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex toward opinionated, non-generic frontend output rather than default boilerplate UI.

**Why now:** The repo gained nearly 2,000 stars this week, coinciding with the rapid mainstream adoption of Claude Code and Codex CLI as everyday coding agents — making style-layer tooling for those agents immediately practical rather than speculative.

**Build with it:** Drop the skill files into your Claude Code or Codex project config, then use them as a pre-generation step that constrains component output before any frontend scaffolding runs.

**What it does:** A TypeScript launcher that routes OpenAI Codex's model picker to ChatGPT Web (including Pro tiers) via a Playwright-driven embedded browser, exposing streaming, images, and local tool calls through MCP without touching your Codex API quota.

**Why now:** The project gained nearly 2,000 stars this week, coinciding with GPT-5 availability and OpenAI's Responses API launch, making quota-free access to top-tier models immediately practical for developers locked out by cost.

**Build with it:** Configure the Full Harness MCP connector in the launcher to give Codex tasks direct access to your local terminal and file tools, then swap the model picker to `ChatGPT Web — Pro` for long-context coding sessions that would otherwise drain Work quota.

**What it does:** OmniRoute is a self-hostable TypeScript gateway that exposes 1,200+ models across 352 providers through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with quota-aware auto-fallback and RTK+Caveman token compression claiming 15–95% reduction.

**Why now:** The repo is trending sharply this week (3,573 stars added), coinciding with active interest in cost-cutting as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor usage bills climb for teams hitting rate limits on paid tiers.

**Build with it:** Point an existing Claude Code or Cursor config at OmniRoute's local endpoint, enable the free-tier rotation across Groq, Mistral, and Gemini pools, and wire the `/dashboard/free-tiers` page into a team Slack alert to surface when a pool nears exhaustion before coding sessions stall.

**What it does:** Agent Reach is a Python CLI and MCP server that lets AI agents scrape and search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and XiaoHongShu without paid APIs, handling auth, anti-bot measures, and HTML-to-readable-text conversion internally.

**Why now:** The repo is trending at #1 on Trendshift this week with 3,392 stars added, coinciding with rapid adoption of MCP-compatible tooling in Claude Code and Cursor workflows.

**Build with it:** Wire it into a Cursor or Claude Code agent via its MCP config surface so your coding assistant can pull live Reddit bug threads or YouTube transcripts directly into context during a debugging session.

**What it does:** book-to-skill ingests a technical PDF, EPUB, DOCX, or document folder and emits a structured agent skill — per-chapter files plus distilled frameworks and decision rules — that Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, or Amp can load on demand instead of stuffing the full text into context.

**Why now:** The repo gained 1,622 stars this week, coinciding with a surge of builder interest in context engineering as a discipline distinct from RAG, making structured skill generation a concrete technique rather than a buzzword.

**Build with it:** Drop `book-to-skill` into a pre-commit or CI step to auto-generate a `/skills` directory from your team's internal architecture docs, then register each skill file as a Claude Code slash command so engineers can query `/adr-guide` or `/api-spec` mid-session without manual copy-paste.
